dimensions.assessment: Affects international air travelers, air carriers, ticket agents, U.S. nationals traveling abroad, and federal foreign policy agencies.
dimensions.evidence: air carrier, foreign air carrier, or ticket agent... passenger listed on the ticket... United States nationals

dimensions.assessment: Imposes administrative certification requirements on airline passengers and creates diplomatic tools and advisory bodies without directly altering domestic civil law beyond travel disclosures.
dimensions.evidence: require the passenger listed on the ticket to certify that the passenger has reviewed the travel advisory

dimensions.assessment: Involves minor administrative and travel expense outlays for advisory council members, with no major spending or revenue figures specified.
dimensions.evidence: allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Robert Levinson Hostage Recovery and Hostage-Taking Accountability Act and title 49 of the United States Code regarding travel advisory ticketing requirements.
dimensions.evidence: amended by inserting after section 306 the following... Chapter 423 of title 49

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory designation frameworks and an advisory council terminating 10 years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The Advisory Council shall terminate on the date that is 10 years after the date of the enactment

missing_information: Exact administrative implementation costs for airlines and federal agencies
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes a State Sponsor of Unlawful or Wrongful Detention designation, requires travel advisory risk certifications for airline passengers travelling to certain countries, creates a non-compensated advisory council, and mandates congressional reports.
